name: office
title: A small office server
summary: One server that receives an office's mail from the Internet, holds its mailboxes and sends what its people write. SPF, the MX check, DKIM and DMARC score what they catch, greylisting defers a first delivery from an unknown sender, a message that reaches the delete threshold after DATA is held in the quarantine rather than refused, an address that keeps failing to sign in is banned and an account that keeps failing is locked, passwords are held to a policy and checked against known breaches, a signed-in person sends only as themselves, and a browser session lasts a working day.
steps: Check that "Require SSL/TLS when authenticating" (the Control Panel's Require TLS before authentication, on the IP ranges page and in the range's dialog) is on for the Internet IP range - a new installation turns it on, an upgraded one keeps what it had (docs/SecureDefaults.md) - or make the submission port STARTTLS-required: that is what refuses a password sent in the clear - SMTP AUTH LOGIN, IMAP LOGIN and POP3 alike - and an IP range is not a setting a profile can write.

Give the submission port (587) STARTTLS with a certificate, or add port 465 with TLS: a port's security is the port's, not a setting, and the checklist's submission item says which port still takes a password in the clear.
Switch each domain's quarantine digest and external-sender tag on in the domain's own settings: both are a domain's choice, and the server has no value of them to set.
Set quarantine_digest_base_url to the address the webmail answers on, or the digest has no links to send.

entries.name: usespf
entries.why: a message from an address its sender's domain has not authorised in its SPF record is scored as a forgery

entries.name: usemxchecks
entries.why: a message whose envelope sender's domain has no MX record, and so cannot be answered, is scored

entries.name: ASDKIMVerificationEnabled
entries.why: a message whose DKIM signature fails to verify is scored, and each signer that verifies is recorded for Authentication-Results and the greylisting bypass list

entries.name: ASDMARCEnabled
entries.why: a message that fails its From domain's own DMARC policy of quarantine or reject is scored, as shipped, and recorded for the aggregate reports

entries.name: spammarkthreshold
entries.why: a message that scores 5 or more is marked as spam, as shipped, written down so the diff shows it

entries.name: spamdeletethreshold
entries.why: a message that scores 20 or more is refused, or held in the quarantine when it is judged after DATA, as shipped and well clear of the mark

entries.name: antispamaddheaderspam
entries.why: a message marked as spam carries X-hMailServer-Spam: YES, as shipped, which a mail client's own junk filter can act on

entries.name: antispamprependsubject
entries.why: the subject of a message marked as spam begins with the text set for it, [SPAM] as shipped, so people see it at a glance

entries.name: usegreylisting
entries.why: a first delivery from an unknown sender, recipient and address is deferred, which a real server retries and most spam software does not

entries.name: BypassGreylistingOnSPFSuccess
entries.why: a message whose SPF passes is not greylisted, as shipped

entries.name: BypassGreylistingOnMailFromMX
entries.why: a message from an address its sender domain's own MX or A record names is not greylisted either

entries.name: QuarantineEnabled
entries.why: a message that reaches the delete threshold after DATA is held for release instead of refused, so a false positive can be put back

entries.name: AuthenticationResultsEnabled
entries.why: the SPF, DKIM and DMARC verdicts are written into each message as Authentication-Results, which a mail client reads and the webmail's brand logos look for

entries.name: AutoBanOnLogonFailureEnabled
entries.why: an address that keeps failing to sign in is banned, as shipped

entries.name: MaxInvalidLogonAttempts
entries.why: an address is banned at its fifth failed sign-in within the window rather than its third, so one mistyped password is not a ban

entries.name: LogonAttemptsWithinMinutes
entries.why: the failures are counted over thirty minutes, as shipped

entries.name: AutoBanMinutes
entries.why: a ban lasts an hour, as shipped, which stops a guessing run and lets a person back in after lunch

entries.name: AccountLockoutThreshold
entries.why: an account that fails ten sign-ins within AccountLockoutWindowMinutes, from any addresses, is locked for AccountLockoutMinutes, thirty minutes each as shipped

entries.name: SmtpAuthenticatedSenderCheck
entries.why: a signed-in account may put in MAIL FROM only its own address, an alias of it, one it verified, or a mailbox that granted it the post right

entries.name: MaxSubmissionsPerIPPerMinute
entries.why: no one address may start more than sixty messages a minute, signed in or not, so a stolen password cannot pour thousands through one

entries.name: PasswordPolicyMinimumLength
entries.why: a password shorter than ten characters is refused wherever one is chosen, and one already set keeps working

entries.name: PasswordPolicyRejectCommon
entries.why: a password on the server's list of the most commonly used ones is refused wherever one is chosen

entries.name: BreachCheckEnabled
entries.why: a password being chosen that is in the published breach corpus is refused, and only the first five characters of its SHA-1 leave the server

entries.name: disconnectinvalidclients
entries.why: an SMTP session that earns more error replies than the limit below is disconnected rather than answered for ever

entries.name: maximumincorrectcommands
entries.why: twenty error replies in one SMTP session, not the hundred shipped, is a probe rather than a confused mail client

entries.name: maxmessagesize
entries.why: SMTP accepts a message of up to 25 MB rather than 20, which most providers accept, so a message sent here can be sent on

entries.name: SessionLifetimeSeconds
entries.why: a webmail, portal or Deck session ends after ten hours however busy, rather than the twelve that apply while it is unset

entries.name: CreateDefaultSpecialUseFolders
entries.why: an account created from now on has Drafts, Sent, Junk and Trash before its first client connects

entries.name: enableattachmentblocking
entries.why: an attachment whose name is on the blocked list, which ships with programs and scripts on it, is replaced with a notice before the message is delivered

entries.name: RecoverDeletedDays
entries.why: a message a person deleted can be put back for two weeks, where nothing deleted is kept as shipped

entries.name: ReputationWatchEnabled
entries.why: once a day the addresses this server knows it sends from are looked up in the block lists receivers use, and a listing is reported, as shipped
